items.question: What does strictNullChecks change compared to legacy TypeScript?
items.answer: null and undefined are not assignable to number, string, object unless explicitly in union or optional. Catches users.find() returning undefined accessed without check. Compile-time only — runtime JSON still delivers null. Cousin of C# nullable reference types.
items.sixtySeconds: null undefined separate types. Narrow before use. Compile time not runtime. C# NRT parallel.

items.question: Compare TypeScript strictNullChecks to C# nullable reference types.
items.answer: Both optional historically, on in modern templates. Both compile-time — runtime null still possible if you lie or parse JSON. C# string? vs TS string | null. Both need validation at API boundaries. Neither replaces runtime guards.
items.sixtySeconds: Both compile-time. Runtime null still hits. Validate boundaries. string? equals string null union.

items.question: When is non-null assertion (!) acceptable?
items.answer: Rarely — when invariant is proven immediately before: getElementById after bootstrap guaranteed root exists, or throw if null right after. Never on fetch json or Redis get. Prefer narrow with if or ?. Code review flags blanket !.
items.sixtySeconds: Only proven invariants. Not on external data. if throw or narrow. Review rejects abuse.

items.question: redis.get returns null on cache miss — type and handle it.
items.answer: Type as string | null or use client typings. if (raw === null) return null or fetch fallback. JSON.parse only after null check. strictNullChecks forces explicit branch — good. Do not ! assert cached value.
items.sixtySeconds: null check before parse. union string null. fallback fetch. guard parsed unknown.

items.question: Explain ?? vs || for default values with strictNullChecks.
items.answer: ?? defaults only null and undefined — preserves 0 and empty string. || treats all falsy including 0 and '' as missing. Use ?? for nullable strings and counts from API. || for intentional falsy-to-default UX.
items.sixtySeconds: ?? null undefined only. || all falsy. ?? for API null. ?. short-circuit access.
